titleEn: Dairy Focus: 12 years of robotic dairying in Westmeath
titleZh: 韦斯特米斯郡12年机器人挤奶实践：从45头育成牛到高产牛群的转型之路
summaryZh: 本文详细介绍了爱尔兰韦斯特米斯郡Fagan家族农场12年来采用Lely A4机器人挤奶系统的经验。农场从2014年安装第一台机器人、挤奶45头育成牛起步，逐步扩大至127头奶牛，2025年每头牛产奶固体达535公斤，跻身Aurivo合作社前15%。文章涵盖机器人系统如何支持兼职工作、优化繁殖与草地管理、降低劳动力成本，以及具体的技术参数（如SCC、EBI、挤奶间隔等），为智慧畜牧从业者提供了可量化的实践参考。
featuredReason: 该案例展示了机器人挤奶系统在爱尔兰家庭农场中的长期应用效果，提供了从设备选型、牛群管理到草地放牧的全链条数据，对智慧畜牧从业者评估自动化投资回报、优化运营流程具有直接参考价值。
contentFull: Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Dairy Focus: 12 years of robotic dairying in Westmeath ![Image 1: Cathal O'Shea By Cathal O'Shea July 25, 2026 4:00 PM](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsauthorcathal-o-shea) Share this article ![Image 2](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsdairy-focus-12-years-of-robotic-dairying-in-westmeath) Michael and Kevin Fagan are milking 127 cows through two Lely A4 Astronaut robotic milking machines alongside Lough Ree in Glasson, Co. Westmeath. Michael always ran a beef and sheep enterprise while working full-time off farm, but in 2014 he decided to take the leap and transition to dairy. It was then installed a single A4 Lely from the Lely Centre Mullingar, and began milking 45 heifers. At the same time, Kevin was sitting his Leaving Cert, but had a desire to return to the farm. ![Image 3](https:images.agriland.ieqgZeTI9ogbWeF2HpSE7c72NFYsZV60flpjmN6zk-8rs:fit:1024:0bg:FFFFFFplainhttps:cdn.agriland.ieuploads202607dji-0600-scaled.jpg) Following the abolishment of quotas, the Fagans expanded their herd size, took on more land, and in 2019 installed their second Lely A4 robot. They climbed to a herd of 140 cows, but underwent a 'hard cull' bringing the herd back to 127 head with a stronger focus on output. Farm performance The robotic system allows the time for Kevin to work off farm as a teacher, but also helps them put more of a focus on getting to know their cows and nailing breeding, as well as other aspects such as grassland management. This focus has allowed them to get their spring-calving British Friesian type herd producing 535kg of milk solids (MS) per cow in 2025 at 4.65% fat and 3.78% protein, off 1.2t of meal. That means that only 11 years after establishing the herd, they were within the top 15% of suppliers for Aurivo co-op in terms of solids. The herd, which has an Economic Breeding Index (EBI) of €163, is also maintaining a 385-day calving interval with an 84% six-week calving rate. ![Image 4](https:images.agriland.ie0EGIic3-gnKFhFd8xixewR2DAG0jn5g4yhcl3rjpU8rs:fit:1024:0bg:FFFFFFplainhttps:cdn.agriland.ieuploads202607img-4444-scaled.jpeg) In 2025, the average somatic cell count (SCC) levels for the year stood at 172,000 cellsml, with 10 cows treated for mastitis, and 33% of the herd receiving only sealer at dry-off. When it comes to grass, the Fagans are stocked at 2.7 LUha and grew just shy of 12t of dry matter (DM)ha in 2025. John McCabe, adviser with the Teagasc-Aurivo Joint Programme, noted that when you look at the herd's production versus meal fed, the Fagans are getting approximately 2kg more of grass into the cows when compared to the Aurivo average, which makes a big difference to the farm's profitability. Lely Robots The Fagans hosted a farm walk alongside Lely Centre Mullingar and Aurivo recently to demonstrate how the system is working for them. They operate an 'A-B-C' grazing system thanks to the Lely Grazeway three-way gate, with cows walking a maximum distance of 950m. The 'A-B-C' system is designed around the farm to allow for three milkings a day. ![Image 5](https:images.agriland.ienDFZ-wNwt23VW3ZxV2ggxRUiJiflLZJk38JKxO-Wgwrs:fit:1024:0bg:FFFFFFplainhttps:cdn.agriland.ieuploads202607img-9256-scaled.jpeg) For example, Block A opens at 2:00a.m with 40% of the cows' daily grass allocation available within. Block B will then open at 10:00a.m with another 40% available, while block C opens at 6:00p.m with 20% available. After a period of time in each block, cows will individually make their way back to the shed where they enter a 'no return gate'. They will only be able to leave the shed through the Grazeway gate once they have been milked. Farmers operating this system will have to move fences: for example; fences moved in 'C' and 'A' while cows are in 'B' during the day. However, labour is drastically reduced, considering milking takes anywhere between two and four hours a day if not more on conventional farms. ![Image 6](https:images.agriland.ietJ5C47SuUL36NYywm8YTeDhDgCVtR8bw5Ompb5ZXXS0rs:fit:1024:0bg:FFFFFFplainhttps:cdn.agriland.ieuploads202607img-9250-scaled.jpeg) The Fagans have a service contract with Lely, and have averaged 2.8 call outs per robot annually over the last five years. Brushes on the robot clean each teat before clusters are applied, with the brushes getting a parasitic acid wash between each cow. The robot uses laser technology for pre- and post-teat spraying, and can also determine when each induvial quarter is milked out to ensure cows are not being under- or over-milked. The same technology is used to determine blank quarters. Each milking is recorded, allowing the Fagan's have up to date SCC readings, milking times, output, and more to make instant informed decisions. ![Image 7](https:images.agriland.ie2ZvX4g7GREsYR8S2uKA7eQqCGCDYU3u8z9uWxu5zHoYrs:fit:1024:0bg:FFFFFFplainhttps:cdn.agriland.ieuploads202607img-9248-scaled.jpeg) A system is installed in which milk can be pumped into separate buckets straight from the robot, which allows each calf get her mother's milk, and helps to stop the spread of diseases such as Johne's, as well as a dump bucket for antibiotic milk. The parlour is also set up with a feed to yield system, allowing the Fagan's to choose how much feed each individual cow is getting. According to Lely, the average robot running cost is €6,970year plus VAT, while electricity works out at approximately €23.10day on a two-robot farm (2024 figure). translationZh:
迈克尔和凯文·费根在位于韦斯特米斯郡格拉森、靠近里湖的农场，通过两台Lely A4 Astronaut机器人挤奶机为127头奶牛挤奶。迈克尔一直从事肉牛和绵羊养殖，同时全职在外工作，但在2014年他决定转型乳业。当时他从Lely Centre Mullingar安装了一台单台Lely A4，开始为45头育成牛挤奶。与此同时，凯文正在参加毕业证书考试，但他渴望回到农场。

配额取消后，费根家族扩大了牛群规模，租用了更多土地，并于2019年安装了第二台Lely A4机器人。他们的牛群数量增至140头，但经过一次“严格淘汰”，牛群数量回落到127头，更加注重产出。

**农场表现**

机器人系统让凯文有时间在外担任教师，同时也帮助他们更专注于了解每头牛、做好育种工作以及草地管理等其他方面。这种专注使他们的春季产犊型英国弗里斯奶牛群在2025年每头牛产奶固体达到535公斤，乳脂率4.65%，乳蛋白率3.78%，精料饲喂量为1.2吨。这意味着，在建立牛群仅11年后，他们在Aurivo合作社的固体物供应中已跻身前15%。该牛群的经济育种指数为163欧元，产犊间隔保持385天，六周产犊率为84%。

2025年，平均体细胞计数水平为172,000个/毫升，有10头牛因乳腺炎接受治疗，33%的牛在干奶期仅使用密封剂。在草地方面，费根家的载畜量为2.7个活重单位/公顷，2025年干物质产量接近12吨/公顷。Teagasc-Aurivo联合项目的顾问约翰·麦凯布指出，从牛群产量与精料饲喂量的对比来看，费根家每头牛从草地获取的干物质比Aurivo平均水平多约2公斤，这对农场的盈利能力产生了重大影响。

**Lely机器人**

费根家最近与Lely Centre Mullingar和Aurivo共同举办了一场农场参观活动，展示这套系统如何为他们工作。他们通过Lely Grazeway三向门运行“A-B-C”放牧系统，奶牛行走的最大距离为950米。“A-B-C”系统围绕农场设计，可实现每天三次挤奶。

例如，A区在凌晨2:00开放，奶牛每日草料配给量的40%可在该区获得；B区在上午10:00开放，再提供40%的草料；C区在下午6:00开放，提供20%的草料。在每个区域停留一段时间后，奶牛会自行返回牛舍，进入“不返回门”。它们只有被挤奶后，才能通过Grazeway门离开牛舍。操作该系统的农民需要移动围栏：例如，当奶牛白天在B区时，移动C区和A区的围栏。然而，劳动力大幅减少，因为传统农场每天挤奶需要两到四个小时甚至更多。

费根家与Lely签订了服务合同，过去五年平均每台机器人每年有2.8次上门服务。机器人上的刷子在套杯前清洁每个乳头，刷子在每头牛之间会进行寄生酸清洗。机器人使用激光技术进行挤奶前和挤奶后的乳头喷雾，并能判断每个乳区何时挤奶完毕，确保奶牛不会挤奶不足或过度。同样的技术用于识别空乳区。每次挤奶都会被记录，使费根家能够获得最新的体细胞计数读数、挤奶时间、产量等信息，从而即时做出明智决策。

系统中安装了一个装置，可以将牛奶直接从机器人泵入单独的桶中，这样每头小牛都能喝到自己母亲的奶，并有助于阻止约翰氏病等疾病的传播，同时还有一个用于丢弃抗生素奶的桶。挤奶厅还配备了按产奶量投喂系统，让费根家可以选择每头牛获得多少饲料。

根据Lely的数据，平均每台机器人的运行成本为每年6,970欧元（不含增值税），而电费在拥有两台机器人的农场中约为每天23.10欧元（2024年数据）。
